note: Biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants consistently cause periatrial leukomalacia-like white matter loss and microcalcifications with typical sparing of anterior temporal poles.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in NOTCH3 produce a distinct clinical and neuroradiological phenotype characterized by spasticity, childhood stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, contrasting with CADASIL.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia.

evidence.text: Patients presenting early with bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants exhibited extensive white matter changes, microbleeds, and microcalcifications, with sparing of the anterior temporal lobes.

source.quote: MRI findings pointed at a small vessel disease, with extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, atrophy, lacunes in the basal ganglia, microbleeds, and microcalcifications. The anterior temporal lobes were spared.
